turn_text: Congressman King, what about the sugar program? It seems to be very different than the others that are within the bill. How did it survive this go around?

Well, it survives, I think, on the strength of the part of its geography and part of it is the protectionism that exists for the sugar production in the rest of the world. It's when you look at the global markets and see the countries that produce sugar in the way they subsidize and manipulate the markets, It puts our U.S. sugar producers at a significant disadvantage. And it's something that I believe we've got to take that apart and start looking at it again when we get another bite at this apple in five years. But the sugar producers are at a distinct disadvantage because other states or other countries are so much manipulating the markets and subsidizing their sugar. And one of the most extreme that I recall, and Cuba's fallen off of the list of major sugar producers, but I recall distortion in there. product down there. There was a time when sugar was worth 6 cents a pound on the global market and the Russians were sending them 52 cents a worth of oil for every 6 cents worth of sugar. That's the worst distortion I've seen, but it exists in percentages of 30 and 40 percent around the world.
